rationale: Identity was properly verified via email and the agent acted on the matching account only. However, there are two major issues: (1) The agent performed multiple writes (updating both orders’ shipping addresses and the user’s default address) without first restating the exact changes and obtaining explicit confirmation, as required by policy. The user’s instruction to “go ahead” is authorization, but the policy requires the agent to state the exact change before proceeding, which it did not. Additionally, the user previously indicated the new address could be found in recent orders; instead the agent chose the profile address (760 Elm) without confirming that this was the new home address, risking updating to the wrong address. (2) For the tablet exchange request, the agent incorrectly identified the “cheapest available” tablet as the 7-inch/128GB/black ($941.03) while a cheaper available option existed (10-inch/64GB/silver at $903.95). The final modification changed to the $941.03 variant, failing the user’s request to switch to the cheapest option. The agent did correctly handle that exchanges aren’t allowed for pending orders and then modified the pending item with proper confirmation, and the stated refund was consistent with tool output. Nonetheless, due to the lack of pre-change confirmation on addresses and the incorrect cheapest-option selection, the conversation does not meet the pass bar.
